```{r cars}
# --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- ---
# Exploring models for resident bird migration
# --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- ---
#
# Goal of this script:
#   This script explores several statistical models for explaining variation in
#   resident bird richness across census block groups or similar spatial units.
#
# Response variable:
#   cbg_resident_richness
#
# Main predictors:
#   traffic_volume       = proxy for road traffic intensity
#   ndvi                 = vegetation greenness / productivity
#   ALAN                 = artificial light at night
#   medincome            = median income
#   precip               = precipitation
#   temp                 = temperature
#   log_checklist_km2    = eBird checklist density or sampling effort proxy
#
# Grouping variable:
#   tract_code           = census tract identifier, used as a random effect
#
# Modeling approaches compared:
#   1. Negative binomial GLMMs using glmmTMB
#   2. Negative binomial GAMs using mgcv
#   3. Alternative treatments of sampling effort:
#        - offset
#        - linear covariate
#        - spline / smooth covariate
# Avonet remove water birds?! -> And re-run the annotation?


library(pacman)
# glmmTMB is used for generalized linear mixed models,
# including negative binomial models with random effects.
library(glmmTMB)
library(splines)
library(mgcv)
p_load(
  "tidycensus",    # Census data access
  "tidyverse",     # Core tidyverse packages: dplyr, ggplot2, readr, etc.
  "dplyr",         # Data wrangling
  "sf",            # Simple features spatial vector data
  "ggplot2",       # Plotting
  "terra",         # Raster and spatial data processing
  "tidyterra",     # ggplot-compatible terra tools
  "tibble",        # Modern data frames
  "lme4",          # Mixed models; useful for comparison and related utilities
  "raster",        # Raster data processing; older spatial raster package
  "MuMIn",         # Model comparison / model selection utilities
  "auk",           # eBird data filtering and processing
  "here",          # Project-relative file paths
  "exactextractr", # Fast raster extraction over polygons
  "modelsummary",  # Model summary tables
  "gtsummary",     # Publication-ready summary tables
  "MASS",          # Statistical modeling utilities, including negative binomial tools
  "sjPlot",        # Model plotting
  "blackmarbler",  # Nighttime lights / Black Marble data tools
  "data.table",    # Fast tabular data handling
  "tigris",        # Census TIGER/Line spatial data
  "glmmTMB",       # Negative binomial GLMMs
  "flextable"      # Formatted tables, often for Word/HTML output
)
library(sjPlot)
library(broom)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(viridisLite)


# --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- ---
# Prepare model data
# --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- ---

tmp_data = st_read('/Users/diegoellis/Downloads/covariate_tmp_data.gpkg')

tmp_model_dat <- tmp_data %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  dplyr::select(
    cbg_resident_richness,
    traffic_volume,
    ndvi,
    ALAN,
    medincome,
    precip,
    temp,
    log_checklist_km2,
    tract_code
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    
    # tract_code is used as a grouping variable for random effects.
    # It should be categorical rather than numeric.
    tract_code = as.factor(tract_code),
    
    # log_checklist_km2 is treated numerically, either as:
    #   - an offset,
    #   - a linear predictor,
    #   - or a smooth / spline term.
    log_checklist_km2 = as.numeric(log_checklist_km2)
  ) %>%
  
  # Remove rows with non-finite values in the model variables.
  # This excludes NA, NaN, Inf, and -Inf values.
  filter(
    if_all(
      c(
        cbg_resident_richness,
        traffic_volume,
        ndvi,
        ALAN,
        medincome,
        precip,
        temp,
        log_checklist_km2
      ),
      ~ is.finite(.)
    ),
    
    # Also remove rows without a valid tract_code.
    !is.na(tract_code)
  )

# Inspect the number of complete observations retained for modeling.
nrow(tmp_model_dat)

# Inspect the number of unique census tracts represented in the model data.
# This matters because tract_code is used as a random effect.
length(unique(tmp_model_dat$tract_code))


# --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- ---
# Model selection
# --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- ---

# --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- ---
# Model 1: Negative binomial GLMM with checklist effort as an offset
# --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- ---
#
# This model treats log_checklist_km2 as an offset.
#
# Interpretation:
#   An offset has its coefficient fixed at 1 on the link scale.
#   Because the link is log, this assumes a proportional relationship between
#   checklist density and expected richness.
#
# Substantive implication:
#   This assumes sampling effort is an exposure-like quantity rather than a
#   predictor whose effect is estimated from the data.
#
# Random effect:
#   (1 | tract_code) allows the model intercept to vary by census tract,
#   accounting for clustering or spatial/social similarity within tracts.

# Checklist as offset, tract as random effect
m_tmb_offset <- glmmTMB(
  cbg_resident_richness ~
    traffic_volume +
    ndvi * ALAN +
    medincome +
    precip +
    temp + 
    offset(log_checklist_km2) +
    (1 | tract_code),
  data = tmp_model_dat,
  family = nbinom2(link = "log")
)


# --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- ---
# Model 2: Negative binomial GLMM with checklist effort as a linear predictor
# --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- ---
#
# This model estimates the coefficient for log_checklist_km2 instead of fixing
# it to 1 as an offset.
#
# Interpretation:
#   The model can learn whether the relationship between checklist density and
#   resident richness is weaker or stronger than the strict offset assumption.
#
# NOTE:
#   The original comment says "randome ffect track"; this appears to mean
#   "random effect tract."

# Effort as predictor variable, randome ffect track
m_tmb_effort_linear <- glmmTMB(
  cbg_resident_richness ~
    traffic_volume +
    ndvi * ALAN +
    medincome +
    precip +
    log_checklist_km2 +
    (1 | tract_code),
  data = tmp_model_dat,
  family = nbinom2(link = "log")
)


# --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- ---
# Model 3: Negative binomial GLMM with checklist effort as a natural spline
# --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- ---
#
# This model allows a nonlinear relationship between checklist density and
# resident richness using a natural spline with 3 degrees of freedom.
#
# ns(log_checklist_km2, df = 3):
#   - Allows curvature in the effect of sampling effort.
#   - Is less flexible than a GAM smooth, but more flexible than a linear term.
#
# This is useful if the relationship between sampling effort and observed
# richness saturates at high effort.

# Testing splines
m_tmb_effort_spline <- glmmTMB(
  cbg_resident_richness ~
    traffic_volume +
    ndvi * ALAN +
    medincome +
    precip +
    ns(log_checklist_km2, df = 3) +
    (1 | tract_code),
  data = tmp_model_dat,
  family = nbinom2(link = "log")
)


# --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- ---
# Model 4: Negative binomial GAM with smooth checklist effort
# --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- ---
#
# This model uses mgcv::gam() rather than glmmTMB.
#
# s(log_checklist_km2):
#   Estimates a smooth, potentially nonlinear effect of checklist density.
#
# s(tract_code, bs = "re"):
#   Represents tract-level random intercepts as a random-effect smooth.
#
# family = nb(link = "log"):
#   Uses a negative binomial response distribution with a log link.
#
# method = "ML":
#   Uses maximum likelihood estimation. This is often used when comparing GAMs
#   by AIC, especially when fixed-effect structures differ.

# GAM
m_gam_effort_smooth <- gam(
  cbg_resident_richness ~
    traffic_volume +
    ndvi * ALAN +
    medincome +
    precip +
    s(log_checklist_km2) +
    s(tract_code, bs = "re"),
  data = tmp_model_dat,
  family = nb(link = "log"),
  method = "ML"
)


# --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- ---
# Model 5: Negative binomial GAM with checklist effort as an offset
# --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- ---
#
# This is the GAM analogue of the glmmTMB offset model.
#
# It combines:
#   - linear fixed effects,
#   - an NDVI × ALAN interaction,
#   - checklist density as an offset,
#   - a tract-level random-effect smooth.

# Gam with offset
m_gam_offset <- gam(
  cbg_resident_richness ~
    traffic_volume +
    ndvi * ALAN +
    medincome +
    precip +
    offset(log_checklist_km2) +
    s(tract_code, bs = "re"),
  data = tmp_model_dat,
  family = nb(link = "log"),
  method = "ML"
)


# --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- ---
# Model 6: Negative binomial GAM with checklist effort as a linear predictor
# --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- ---
#
# This is the GAM analogue of the glmmTMB linear-effort model.
#
# It differs from m_gam_effort_smooth by treating log_checklist_km2 as a linear
# predictor rather than as a smooth term.

# Gam with linear effort
m_gam_effort_linear <- gam(
  cbg_resident_richness ~
    traffic_volume +
    ndvi * ALAN +
    medincome +
    precip +
    log_checklist_km2 +
    s(tract_code, bs = "re"),
  data = tmp_model_dat,
  family = nb(link = "log"),
  method = "ML"
)

# --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- ---
# Model 7: Partially smoothed GAM with tensor interaction
# --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- ---
#
# This model keeps most predictors linear but adds a nonlinear interaction
# between NDVI and ALAN using ti().
#
# ti(ndvi, ALAN, k = c(5, 5)):
#   Estimates a tensor-product interaction between NDVI and ALAN.
#   This allows the effect of one variable to vary nonlinearly with the other.
#
# Difference from ndvi * ALAN:
#   ndvi * ALAN fits a linear-by-linear interaction.
#   ti(ndvi, ALAN) allows a smoother, more flexible interaction surface.
#
# s(log_checklist_km2):
#   Allows nonlinear sampling-effort adjustment.
#
# s(tract_code, bs = "re"):
#   Accounts for tract-level clustering.

m_gam_full_smooth <- gam(
  cbg_resident_richness ~
    traffic_volume +
    ndvi +
    ALAN +
    ti(ndvi, ALAN, k = c(5, 5)) +
    medincome +
    precip +
    s(log_checklist_km2) +
    s(tract_code, bs = "re"),
  data = tmp_model_dat,
  family = nb(link = "log"),
  method = "ML"
)


# --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- ---
# Optional model diagnostics for m_gam_full_smooth
# --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- ---
#
# These lines are commented out in the original code.
#
# summary():
#   Displays estimated coefficients, smooth terms, significance tests,
#   estimated degrees of freedom, deviance explained, and other model details.
#
# gam.check():
#   Checks basis dimensions, residual patterns, and other GAM diagnostics.
#
# AIC():
#   Returns Akaike Information Criterion for model comparison.

# summary(m_gam_full_smooth)
# gam.check(m_gam_full_smooth)
# AIC(m_gam_full_smooth)


# --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- ---
# Assemble models into a named list for comparison
# --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- ---

model_list <- list(
  "TMB offset" = m_tmb_offset,
  "TMB linear effort" = m_tmb_effort_linear,
  "TMB spline effort" = m_tmb_effort_spline,
  "GAM offset" = m_gam_offset,
  "GAM linear effort" = m_gam_effort_linear,
  "GAM full smooth" = m_gam_full_smooth
)

# --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- ---
# Compare models using likelihood-based criteria
# --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- ---
#
# For each model, extract:
#   - model name
#   - number of observations
#   - effective degrees of freedom
#   - log-likelihood
#   - AIC
#   - BIC
#
# Then compute:
#   delta_AIC:
#     Difference between each model's AIC and the lowest AIC in the set.
#
#   AIC_weight:
#     Approximate relative support for each model among the candidate set.
#
# Important:
#   AIC comparisons are most interpretable when models are fit to the same
#   response variable, same data, and comparable likelihood frameworks.
#   Comparing glmmTMB and mgcv models can be informative but should be done
#   cautiously because the implementations and effective degrees of freedom
#   may differ.

model_compare <- purrr::map_dfr(
  names(model_list),
  function(nm) {
    
    # Retrieve the model object associated with the current model name.
    m <- model_list[[nm]]
    
    # Store model-level comparison statistics in a tibble.
    tibble(
      model = nm,
      nobs = nobs(m),
      df = attr(logLik(m), "df"),
      logLik = as.numeric(logLik(m)),
      AIC = AIC(m),
      BIC = BIC(m)
    )
  }
) %>%
  
  # Sort models from best to worst according to AIC.
  arrange(AIC) %>%
  
  # Compute AIC deltas and Akaike weights.
  mutate(
    delta_AIC = AIC - min(AIC),
    AIC_weight = exp(-0.5 * delta_AIC) / sum(exp(-0.5 * delta_AIC))
  )

# Print the full model comparison table.
model_compare

# Create a formatted flextable version of the model comparison table.
# Numeric columns are rounded for readability.
model_compare %>%
  mutate(
    across(c(logLik, AIC, BIC, delta_AIC, AIC_weight), round, 3)
  ) %>%
  flextable()

# Print a smaller model comparison table focused on AIC results.
model_compare %>%
  dplyr::select(model, AIC, delta_AIC, AIC_weight)


# --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- ---
# Residual diagnostics using DHARMa
# --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- ---

# DHARMa provides simulation-based residual diagnostics for fitted models.
# This is especially useful for GLMMs and non-Gaussian models where ordinary
# residual diagnostics can be misleading.
library(DHARMa)


# Define a helper function to run the same DHARMa diagnostics on multiple models.
check_dharma <- function(model, model_name) {
  
  # Print a clear header so the output can be linked to the model being checked.
  cat("\n\n====================\n")
  cat(model_name, "\n")
  cat("====================\n")
  
  # Simulate scaled residuals from the fitted model.
  # n = 1000 sets the number of simulations used to construct the residual
  # distribution.
  res <- simulateResiduals(model, n = 1000)
  
  # Test whether residuals are uniformly distributed.
  # A significant result may indicate lack of fit.
  print(testUniformity(res))
  
  # Test for overdispersion or underdispersion not captured by the model.
  print(testDispersion(res))
  
  # Test whether the model predicts the observed number of zeros adequately.
  print(testZeroInflation(res))
  
  # Plot core DHARMa diagnostic plots.
  plot(res)
  
  # Plot residuals against sampling effort to check whether residual structure
  # remains along the checklist-density gradient.
  plotResiduals(res, tmp_model_dat$log_checklist_km2)
  
  # Return the residual object invisibly so it can be stored and inspected later
  # without printing additional output.
  invisible(res)
}


# Run DHARMa diagnostics on selected candidate models.
#
# These objects allow later inspection of residual diagnostics without rerunning
# the simulations.
res_tmb_linear <- check_dharma(m_tmb_effort_linear, "TMB linear effort")
res_tmb_spline <- check_dharma(m_tmb_effort_spline, "TMB spline effort")

res_gam_full <- check_dharma(m_gam_full_smooth, "GAM full smooth")


# --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- ---
# Plot model estimates: GLMM linear effort model
# --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- ---
#
# plot_model(..., type = "est"):
#   Plots coefficient estimates.
#
# transform = "exp":
#   Exponentiates coefficients from the log scale.
#   For negative binomial models with a log link, exponentiated coefficients
#   can be interpreted approximately as incidence-rate ratios.
#
# show.values = TRUE:
#   Adds numeric estimate labels to the plot.

plot_model(
  m_tmb_effort_linear,
  type = "est",
  transform = "exp",
  show.values = TRUE,
  value.offset = 0.3,
  title = "Resident species richness model",
  axis.title = "Incidence-rate ratio"
)


# --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- ---
# Compare coefficient estimates between two GLMM effort specifications
# --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- ---
#
# This plot compares the fixed-effect estimates from:
#   1. the linear checklist-effort GLMM
#   2. the spline checklist-effort GLMM
#
# This helps assess whether changing the effort adjustment meaningfully changes
# the estimated effects of the substantive predictors.

plot_models(
  m_tmb_effort_linear,
  m_tmb_effort_spline,
  transform = "exp",
  show.values = TRUE,
  m.labels = c("Linear checklist effect", "Spline checklist effect"),
  title = "Comparison of resident richness GLMMs",
  axis.title = "Incidence-rate ratio"
)


# --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- ---
# Predicted richness across checklist density: linear GLMM
# --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- ---
#
# This visualizes the model-implied relationship between sampling effort
# and predicted resident richness, holding other predictors at their defaults
# as defined internally by sjPlot.

# Predicted richness across checklist density
plot_model(
  m_tmb_effort_linear,
  type = "pred",
  terms = "log_checklist_km2",
  title = "Predicted resident richness across sampling effort",
  axis.title = c("Log checklist density", "Predicted resident richness")
)


# --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- ---
# Predicted richness across checklist density: spline GLMM
# --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- ---
#
# This is the analogous prediction plot for the spline version of the effort
# model. It is useful for checking whether the effort-richness relationship
# appears nonlinear.

# For the spline version:
  
plot_model(
  m_tmb_effort_spline,
  type = "pred",
  terms = "log_checklist_km2",
  title = "Predicted resident richness with spline effort adjustment",
  axis.title = c("Log checklist density", "Predicted resident richness")
)


# --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- ---
# NDVI × ALAN interaction plot for the GLMM
# --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- ---
#
# terms = c("ndvi", "ALAN [meansd]"):
#   Predicts across NDVI while showing ALAN at representative values,
#   typically mean and +/- 1 SD, depending on sjPlot/ggeffects handling.
#
# This plot helps evaluate whether the association between greenness and
# resident richness changes under different artificial-light conditions.
  
# NDVI × ALAN interaction plot
  
plot_model(
  m_tmb_effort_linear,
  type = "pred",
  terms = c("ndvi", "ALAN [meansd]"),
  title = "NDVI × ALAN interaction",
  axis.title = c("NDVI", "Predicted resident richness")
)
    
    
# sjPlot is loaded again here. This is redundant because it was already loaded
# with p_load(), but it does not change the model behavior.
library(sjPlot)
  

# --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- ---
# Plot model estimates for GAM smooth-effort model
# --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- ---
#
# --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- ---
# Predicted richness across checklist density: GAM smooth-effort model
# --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- ---


# --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- ---
# GAM prediction plot for ALAN across NDVI levels
# --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- ---
#
# terms = c("ALAN", "ndvi [meansd]"):
#   Predicts resident richness across ALAN values while holding NDVI at
#   representative values, typically the mean and +/- 1 SD.
#
# This plot asks a slightly different interaction question from the earlier
# NDVI-focused plot:
#   How does the predicted ALAN effect vary across greener vs. less green areas?


# --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- ---
# Store prediction plots as objects
# --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- ---
#
# Saving plots as objects makes it easier to:
#   - print them later,
#   - combine them with patchwork/cowplot,
#   - save them with ggsave(),
#   - or compare them visually in sequence.
#
# p_tmb_effort:
#   Predicted effort effect from the GLMM with a linear checklist-density term.
#

  # p_gam_effort <- plot_model(

# p_gam_effort:
#   Predicted effort effect from the GAM with a smooth checklist-density term.

# p_tmb_effort <- plot_model(

#   type = "pred",
#   terms = "log_checklist_km2",

#   axis.title = c("Log checklist density", "Predicted resident richness")
# )

  
# Print the stored prediction plots.
# p_tmb_effort
# p_gam_effort

plot_models(
  m_tmb_offset,
  m_tmb_effort_linear,
  m_tmb_effort_spline,
  show.values = TRUE,
  show.p = TRUE,
  transform = NULL,
  m.labels = c(
    "Offset",
    "Linear effort",
    "Spline effort"
  ),
  title = "Coefficient comparison across resident richness models",
  axis.title = "Estimate on log scale"
)

gam_coef <- bind_rows(
  tidy(m_gam_offset, parametric = TRUE, conf.int = TRUE) %>%
    mutate(model = "GAM offset"),
  
  tidy(m_gam_effort_linear, parametric = TRUE, conf.int = TRUE) %>%
    mutate(model = "GAM linear effort"),
  
  tidy(m_gam_full_smooth, parametric = TRUE, conf.int = TRUE) %>%
    mutate(model = "GAM full smooth")
) %>%
  filter(term != "(Intercept)") %>%
  mutate(
    sig = case_when(
      p.value < 0.001 ~ "***",
      p.value < 0.01  ~ "**",
      p.value < 0.05  ~ "*",
      p.value < 0.1   ~ ".",
      TRUE ~ ""
    )
  )

ggplot(gam_coef, aes(x = estimate, y = term, color = model)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray50") +
  geom_pointrange(
    aes(xmin = conf.low, xmax = conf.high),
    position = position_dodge(width = 0.5)
  ) +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = sig),
    position = position_dodge(width = 0.5),
    hjust = -0.4,
    color = "black",
    size = 5
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(values = viridisLite::viridis(3)) +
  labs(
    title = "Parametric GAM coefficient comparison",
    x = "Estimate on log scale",
    y = NULL,
    color = "Model"
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```
